children: Palm oil rises in Asian trading amid bargain hunting, with the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for November delivery up 37 ringgit at 4,851 ringgit a ton. However, the crude palm oil market could remain under pressure as rising Malaysian inventories and weaker export demand weigh on sentiment, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. Technical analysis suggests CPO futures remain bearish, with technical rebound facing resistance around 4,891 ringgit-4,920 ringgit a ton, it adds. AmInvestment Bank expects palm oil prices to face support at 4,740 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
